title: Simonetti back for second stint as Dover football coach - NewsBreak
text: DOVER — Rudy Simonetti hasn’t been Dover High’s head football coach since 2020. But he was never far away from the Senators or the sport, either. And, when Dover found itself without a coach just before the start of the season, officials realized their solution was right there ready to step back in. On Wednesday night, Dover hired the 42-year-old Simonetti back at as its head football coach 11 days before the beginning of preseason camp. He led the program, from 2016-20, finishing with arecord 22-25. In 2018, Dover went 9-2 after losing to eventual state champion Sussex Central, 21-20, in the DIAA Division I state semifinals. It was the program’s first state tourney appearance since 2013 and Simonetti was named the Henlopen Conference Coach of the Year. “Dover has become my home since moving down here from Jersey,” said Simonetti. “I’m invested in the community. It was just about being patient and waiting I guess for the right opportunity to break open. “I’ve been around a lot of good people the last couple years. That has prepared me to take on this challenge.” “Rudy was a good person to have in the right place at the right time,” said Dover athletic director Kevin Turner. “I feel really good about the situation. “Having Rudy, who’s so familiar with the school, the kids and local football, we lucked out on this one for sure.” Simonetti has taught at Dover for all but two years since he first moved from New Jersey in 2016. Since 2021, he’s been an assistant coach at both Smyrna and Polytech before assisting former Senators coach Chip Knapp two years ago. He was planning to be an assistant at Caesar Rodney this fall and had started working with the Riders. Maurice Paulk was Dover’s head coach last season, leading Dover to a 3-6 record. He stepped down last week, leaving Dover to have to quickly find a replacement. Dover had only five head football coach between 1986 and 2020. That list includes Simonetti, Dante Jones, Carlton Brown, Darwin Manges and Jim Oxford. The Senators open the season on Aug. 29 at West Catholic, Pa. High. As a history teacher, Simonetti already knows many of the current players. He talked with several of them informally on Wednesday. “This is not normal for them either, obviously,” said Simonetti. “Camp starts in a week and a half. They were excited, I guess, to have the issue resolved. And they were just anxious to get going.” “Everything I got back was positive feedback, which I’m not surprised,” said Turner. “I could tell he was really excited. He’s already working.”
